title: A map of coherent modules injective, surjective or bijective on one stalk is so on a neighbourhood
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ a homomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $x\in X$, with stalks and stalk maps $\varphi_x:\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal F_x$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; for an open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal F|_U$ is the restriction ($\mathcal F|_U(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ open). (1) If $\mathcal F_x=0$, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ with $\mathcal F|_U=0$. (2) If $\varphi_x$ is injective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is injective (on the sections over every open $V\subseteq U$). (3) If $\varphi_x$ is surjective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U$ is surjective (as a map of sheaves). (4) If $\varphi_x$ is bijective, there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $\varphi|_U:\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal F|_U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y3 (label lemma-local-isomorphism); its proof cites Modules, Lemmas finite-type-surjective-on-stalk, finite-type-stalk-zero and finite-type-to-coherent-injective-on-stalk
